newsitem.title: USA: GM Q1 retail incentives rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: GM Q1 retail incentives rise sharply.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday its first quarter retail incentives rose sharply over last year in both North America and in Europe, reflecting highly competitive market conditions.

GM said its North American retail incentives rose to $860 per vehicle in the first quarter from $598 a year earlier. In Europe, GM's incentives rose to $622 per vehicle during the first quarter from $443 a year earlier.

Stronger volume and new models allowed GM to report first quarter net income from continuing operations of $1.8 billion, or $2.30 a share, up from strike-crippled year-ago earnings of $800 million, or $0.93 a share.

GM utilized 95.3 percent of its U.S. and Canadian production capacity during the first quarter, compared with 69.1 percent in the year-earlier period. The automaker's North American wholesale vehicle sales rose to 1.4 million from 1.17 million a year earlier.

Nonetheless, GM lost retail market share in the United States, capturing 30.2 percent of the combined car and truck market in the first quarter, compared with 31.2 percent a year earlier. In Europe, GM's market share fell to 11.5 percent from 12.0 percent a year ago, and in Latin America it fell to 16 percent from 17.2 percent a year ago.

Despite the introduction of new models aimed at retail buyers, GM said it sold 26.5 percent of its cars to fleet buyers in the United States during the period, versus 25 percent a year ago. GM sold 13.6 percent of its trucks to fleets, up from 11.3 percent in the year-ago period.
GM said its U.S. dealer inventories of cars fell to an 81-day supply during the first quarter from 84 days a year earlier, while truck inventories rose to a 91-day supply from 81 days a year earlier.
